source.title: A Data-Centric Approach to Generalizable Speech Deepfake Detection
source.authors: Wen Huang; Yuchen Mao; Yanmin Qian

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies data-scaling relationships for speech deepfake detection, a different modality and task from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports power-law fits for detection error versus source and generator diversity. Those results bear on V5 as evidence about scaling in speech, but do not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute. Its DOSS mixing comparisons and benchmark EER/ACC results are not rows for the claim versions unless they are part of the reported diversity-scaling fits.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of a speech deepfake classifier's error (an 'optimality gap' in CDE) against the number of distinct source or generator datasets. That is a related but different construct: the axis is a count of data domains (1–8 or 1–16), not parameters, tokens or compute, and the measure is a fine-tuned classifier's error, not held-out pretraining loss. It does not test V1–V7 as stated; its own scaling-type findings go under fits_no_version. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that SDD generalization follows predictable power laws in source and generator diversity, that diversity matters more than raw volume, and that DOSS mixing beats naive aggregation.
record.recipe_differences: Studies speech deepfake detection scaling against data-composition variables and uses CDE, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling axes are source diversity and generator diversity; the experiments also vary data usage percentage. The paper says EER and ACC can behave differently across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned XLS-R-300M detection error (the CDE 'optimality gap') fits a power law in the number of distinct sources (R2=0.998, 4 points) and generators (R2=0.93, 5 points).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fine-tuned classifiers, out-of-domain error scales as a power law in the number of distinct training data domains.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed number of diverse units, raising data volume (6.25%→100% usage) gives diminishing returns that plateau. For example, 8 sources at 12.5% beat 1 source at 100% (Finding 1, Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data diversity, rather than volume, drives fine-tuning data scaling; volume scaling saturates.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling the XLS-R backbone from 300M to 1B parameters reduces average out-of-domain EER from 2.14% to 1.65% (~23%, Table 2). This rests on two points only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger pretrained backbones improve fine-tuned detection, but no scaling law is fitted.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025), as stated in the supplied metadata
record.problems: The scaling-law tests use one fixed 300M-parameter backbone and CDE rather than held-out cross-entropy. The power-law fit values are presented in Figure 2; the paper's limitations say it does not explore a broad range of model sizes or computational budgets.
record.rows_left_out: No other results are included: DOSS strategy comparisons and public-benchmark or commercial-API outcomes (Tables 1–3 and 8–10) report detection performance for different training mixtures or models, not the claim's language-model loss laws.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss; no scaling in parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No power law in parameters, tokens or compute for speech or fine-tuning. The scaling axes are domain-diversity counts only.
Only two model sizes (300M, 1B) on downstream detection; no scaling trend fitted.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'supports' label is removed. V5 concerns the same power-law form, implicitly in parameters, tokens or compute (or repeated data and transfer). Here the scaled quantity is a domain count over at most ~1 order of magnitude, using a metric whose 'optimality gap' transformation is not defined in the text. If curators read V5 broadly enough to include any data-composition power law, R1–R2 would at most give weak T3 support, limited by few points and a narrow range. DOSS and benchmark tables are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss or scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small language-model runs to larger runs.
No compute-budget allocation between language-model parameters and tokens.
No comparison of language-model architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.

Tests speech deepfake detection performance against source and generator diversity, not language-model pretraining loss or the same parameter/token/compute scaling axes. Does not test image/video models, repeated data, or transfer.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship to language-model pretraining loss.
Does not compare language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, and does not test departures from language-model power laws.

rows.subject: XLS-R-300M
rows.operation_detail: Fit optimality gap (CDE) against number of source datasets.
rows.note: Figure 2 describes the plotted averages and min/max range across experimental trials and identifies this fit as using full data usage. The text states that CDE follows a predictable power law. This is a speech-detection metric and source-diversity axis, not language-model loss or parameter/token/compute scaling.
rows.check: The axis is the number of source datasets (1,2,4,8), not parameters, tokens or compute, and the measure is classifier error. The fit covers only 4 points within one order of magnitude. The 'optimality gap' is undefined in the text, and its positive exponent (0.26) cannot be read against falling error without that definition. Belongs in fits_no_version.

relation.reason: The related-work section discusses established scaling laws and motivates an analogous investigation of speech detection data composition; the reported fits measure a different construct.

tranche.reason: The fitted outcome is a detection-error composite against source or generator diversity, rather than loss against parameters, tokens or compute. These domain-count fits do not establish the specified scaling-law versions.

source_check.notes: Both equations and R² values are explicitly printed in the extracted figure legends. Section 3.1 defines CDE as the harmonic mean of EER and 1−ACC, but does not separately define an optimality-gap transformation; the extracted exponents appear positive.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Speech deepfake detection, CDE versus source or generator diversity at full data usage
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports power-law fits for CDE against both diversity axes (R1–R2); this is evidence of a scaling relationship in speech detection, but not a direct test of language-model loss scaling.
